name: CT-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joe Courtney has won easily in a D+4 district and holds a large cash advantage
Polymarket prices Courtney at about 96% to win
No public polls or expert ratings, so the forecast leans on fundamentals
Republican George Austin's modest fundraising limits his ability to compete
model.rationale: Courtney combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, and a roughly three-to-one fundraising edge, while markets price him near certain. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays at a double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or significant outside spending against Courtney would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern Connecticut's 2nd District leans Democratic by about four points, and six-term incumbent Joe Courtney is seeking reelection with a strong financial position. He has raised roughly $760,000 and holds over $600,000 on hand, while Republican challenger George Austin has raised about $284,000 with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Courtney roughly a 96% chance of winning. The forecast expects a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin, with the main risk being the absence of direct polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive race.
